selected_case.selection_reason: LaunchDarkly tests the opposite of Watermelon and Iris: a stable high-evidence entity where state-first generation should stay light and avoid inventing ambiguity.

baseline.synthesis_excerpt: The baseline sees a coherent owned narrative around runtime control for releases, AI behavior, and customer experience, but still repeats self-description caveats and generic decision framing.
baseline.core_problem: Entity ambiguity is low, so the main failure is not composition identity. The baseline mostly needs caveat discipline, evidence binding, and less generic strategic advice.

entity_ambiguity.rule: Do not introduce false ambiguity. Treat launchdarkly.com as the stable primary entity unless explicit contrary evidence appears.

primary_tension.summary: The entity signal is stable and the product story is clear. The actual tension is between strong owned positioning and uneven external/evidence URL coverage, especially around vitality and uncited findings.

owned_or_primary_surface.supports: Owned positioning around automation, feature management, runtime control, releases, AI behavior, and customer experience.
owned_or_primary_surface.boundary: Owned positioning supports message clarity, not external market validation by itself.

owned_or_primary_surface.supports: Owned platform page with reliability and scale claims.
owned_or_primary_surface.boundary: Claims such as uptime and flag evaluations need external corroboration before becoming proof.

external_or_third_party.supports: Third-party update signal about feature restoration capability.
external_or_third_party.boundary: Supports product activity, not broad market momentum.
Useful external evaluation signal; do not overstate without quote-level detail.
Supports market-recognition context, not preference or superiority.

external_or_third_party.supports: Press-release signal about leadership expansion and AI tailwinds.
external_or_third_party.boundary: Press-release framing should be attributed; it is not independent proof of growth quality.

missing_or_uncited.rule: Missing evidence URLs should trigger narrower findings, not broader caveats.

can_state_as_observation: LaunchDarkly has a stable primary entity at launchdarkly.com.
The owned surface clearly uses runtime control, feature management, releases, AI behavior, and customer experience language.
Some external references exist through ReleaseBot, Rollgate, PostHog, and GlobeNewswire.
The payload overuses self-description caveats and generic Decision Space.
can_state_as_interpretation: The main narrative can be written as a stable product-positioning case, not an entity-ambiguity case.
The strongest safe tension is proof distribution: owned claims are clear, but evidence support varies by dimension.
must_remain_uncertain: Whether owned reliability and scale claims are independently verified.
How much external market momentum exists beyond the cited third-party references.
Whether AI-tailwind language reflects durable positioning or current campaign emphasis.
requires_human_review: Any production claim that LaunchDarkly is externally validated as category leader.
Any recommendation to shift strategy between AI, feature management, or runtime control.
Any use of press-release claims as independent proof.
must_not_infer: A weak brand simply because some findings lack evidence URLs.
Market leadership from owned claims alone.
A strategic need to change positioning when the baseline entity story is already clear.

coordination_rules: Keep state-first light because the entity is stable.
Centralize caveat discipline around evidence coverage, not entity ambiguity.
Use external evidence only where it actually supports activity or market context.

dimension_plan.coherencia: Confirm the stable owned narrative and avoid turning AI language into speculative strategy.
dimension_plan.diferenciacion: Treat runtime control as the owned differentiating frame; separate owned claim from proof.
dimension_plan.percepcion: Use external references as recognition context, not perception proof.
dimension_plan.presencia: Show strong owned presence and evidence gaps without generic recommendations.
dimension_plan.vitalidad: Use product updates, press release, and competitive references as activity signals with attribution.

generated_state_first_findings.global_caveat: State-first reading treats LaunchDarkly as a stable, low-ambiguity entity. The trial should not add entity complexity; it should only tighten evidence boundaries and reduce repeated caveats.

coherencia.title: The core story is already stable
coherencia.finding: LaunchDarkly's owned surface consistently frames the company around runtime control, releases, AI behavior, customer experience, automation, and feature management. The state-first task is not to discover a hidden contradiction; it is to keep that coherent story from being diluted by repeated self-description caveats and generic strategy choices.
coherencia.uncertainty: Owned positioning is clear; independent validation of scale and performance claims still requires external proof.

diferenciacion.title: Runtime control is the differentiating frame
diferenciacion.finding: The safest differentiation reading is that LaunchDarkly wants to own runtime control across feature releases, AI behavior, and customer experience. That is specific enough to keep. The report should not convert it into a recommendation about whether to emphasize AI or feature management unless additional strategic evidence supports that choice.
diferenciacion.uncertainty: The frame is visible, but category strength and customer preference are not proven by owned copy alone.

percepcion.title: External references support recognition, not full perception
percepcion.finding: ReleaseBot, Rollgate, and PostHog give LaunchDarkly external context: product-update visibility, audit/reference material, and competitive comparison. These sources are enough to avoid treating the brand as purely self-described, but they do not by themselves prove broad market sentiment.
percepcion.uncertainty: External perception should remain bounded to the cited sources.

presencia.title: Owned presence is strong; evidence coverage is uneven
presencia.finding: LaunchDarkly's owned presence is clear and consistent, but several baseline findings lack evidence URLs. State-first generation should not treat missing URLs as a brand weakness. It should treat them as report-evidence coverage gaps and keep those findings narrower.
presencia.uncertainty: Evidence gaps belong to the report layer unless additional sources show actual presence weakness.

vitalidad.title: Activity signals exist, but should stay attributed
vitalidad.finding: The evidence set includes an owned blog/update signal, a third-party update mention, competitive context, and a GlobeNewswire leadership-expansion press release. Together they support recent activity around AI, platform capability, and market context. The safer reading is active but attributed vitality, not an unqualified claim of accelerated growth.
vitalidad.uncertainty: Press-release claims remain attributed; external activity does not automatically prove market momentum.

against_baseline.specificity: state_first slightly wins by preserving LaunchDarkly's actual frame instead of turning every finding into a strategy fork.
against_baseline.evidence_binding: state_first wins because it separates owned claims, third-party references, and report evidence gaps.
against_baseline.entity_coherence: baseline and state_first both preserve a stable entity; state_first must not add false ambiguity.
against_baseline.caveat_discipline: state_first wins by centralizing evidence-coverage caution.
against_baseline.overreach_risk: state_first wins only if it stays light; overstructuring would be a failure.

against_watermelon.shared_pattern: All cases benefit from caveat and evidence-boundary discipline.
against_watermelon.difference: Watermelon needed entity ambiguity as the governing condition; LaunchDarkly does not.
against_watermelon.value_level: State-first helps less dramatically here. The correct behavior is controlled restraint, not a heavy rewrite.

cross_case_synthesis.where_state_first_helps: It helps across all cases by coordinating evidence boundaries before prose.
cross_case_synthesis.where_it_overreaches: It overreaches in LaunchDarkly if it invents ambiguity or tension to justify itself.
cross_case_synthesis.where_it_should_stay_inactive: It should stay light for stable-entity, well-evidenced brands where the baseline already has a coherent story.

what_failed: The improvement is smaller than Watermelon or Iris.
A heavy state-first rewrite would be worse than the baseline.
The trial still required manual generation.
Some baseline findings already had adequate entity coherence.
verdict.biggest_improvement: State-first generation shows when to stay light: it improves evidence discipline without inventing entity ambiguity.
verdict.biggest_remaining_risk: The method could become self-justifying and add complexity to healthy cases.
